--- title: "Module 1: Foundations" ---
![](../../src/images/hex_complex.png){.intro_image fig-alt="Logo"} ## Module overview In this module, we will cover the basic concepts and primary tools that we will use throughout these lessons. We will not be working with much real data yet (but soon will!). Instead, this module is really dedicated to developing a conceptual understanding of R that we can build on throughout these lessons. It is divided into four sections: - **1.2 Getting started**: This section provides the [*necessary*]{style="color:red;"} steps that you must take *prior* to completing the content of this module. - **1.3 Objects**: This lesson is an enhanced review of functions, environments, and common data objects. Special emphasis is placed on developing a vocabulary that will give you the flexibility to address and understand more complex operations. - **1.4 Importing, exploring, and exporting data**: Here, we will review how to import and export `.csv` and `.rds` files, learn how to read `.xlsx` files, and describe exploratory steps that should be taken *every time* you read a file. - **1.5 Assignments**: In this lesson, we will review global (and "local") assignments, and you will learn the benefits and pitfalls of their usage. Along the way, you will learn how to use magrittr's pipe operator, and I will provide recommendations to improve your R workflow and manage your global environment. **Problem set**: [Problem set 1: R foundations](../../problem_sets/problem_set_1/problem_set_1.qmd) *Note: We will quickly build on the content herein, so please be sure to read/view all content in the order that it appears!* ## About this module's data In this module, we will use the following data files in our exercises: **Global populations and CO2 emissions** (`API_EN.ATM.CO2E.PC_DS2_en_csv_v2_2764620.csv`): These data were compiled by the [World Bank DataBank](https://databank.worldbank.org/home.aspx){target="_blank"} and provide information on the emissions of greenhouse gases and the populations of countries around the world. Neither the tabular data nor the name of the file were modified from the original version. **Iris** (`iris.csv`, `iris.rds`): This is Edgar Anderson's famous dataset that provides the measurements of flowers of three species of iris, *Iris setosa*, *I. versicolor*, and *I. virginica*. See `?iris` for more information. **My Covid garden** (`my_covid_garden.xlsx`, `my_covid_garden.csv`, `my_covid_garden.rds`, `badNameDataFrame.csv`): These are tabular datasets (in different formats) that describe a pretty unsuccessful raised bed garden at my home in Takoma Park, Maryland. **Portal rodents** (`portal.csv`, `portal.xlsx`): These datasets provide measurements taken in a long-term study (the Portal project) on rodent traits in Portal, Arizona. The provided data were collected in a fixed grid established in 1977 and include when an individual was measured, where the measurement occurred, the sex and species of the individual, and their hindfoot length. You can read more about this study and the data they collected at this [link](https://portal.weecology.org/){target="_blank"}. I intentionally made the data a good bit messier than the original version. ## Readings and resources Please review the following resources: - **[Style guide](../resources/course_style_guide.qmd){target="_blank"}**: Modern standards in R coding compel us to generate code that is consistent, parsimonious, and communicable. This tutorial provides the set of code formatting rules that I ask you to follow in these lessons. The provided rules are closely aligned with the tidyverse style guide. - **[Solving problem sets](../resources/solving_and_submitting_problem_sets.qmd){target="_blank"}**: This brief tutorial provides tips and tricks for completing the (notoriously difficult) problem sets with as little pain as possible. ### Optional readings :::{style="margin-top:16px;"} - Wickham & Grolemund (1^st^ edition): - [18.1-18.2: Pipes](https://r4ds.had.co.nz/pipes.html) - [11.1-11.2: Data import](https://r4ds.had.co.nz/data-import.html) - **Cheat sheets:** I *strongly* recommend printing the cheat sheets to have a handy reference for understanding functions and how they are used (*Note: Please use [this link](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/translations.html) to access translated cheat sheets*)! - [RStudio IDE](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/rstudio-ide.pdf) - [Data import (readr)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/cheatsheets/main/data-import.pdf) - [Base R](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/base-r.pdf) - [Best Practice for R](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/R-best-practice.pdf) ::: ## Reference ::: panel - **Arguments**: A value supplied to a function that modifies its behavior when the function runs. - **Assignment (noun)**: A reference that R uses to call data from your computer’s memory (also called "name"). - **Assignment (verb)**: The act of associating a name with an object (typically to the global environment). - **Assignment operator**: A function used to assign an object to a name. - **Atomic vector**: A one-dimensional, homogeneous data object (a set of values of the same class). - **Attributes**: Information about the values of an object that is not contained in the values themselves. - **Character**: A symbol or set of symbols from a given alphabet (note: also includes numbers and punctuation). - **Child**: An object whose name is stored as a reference in a parent object. - **Class**: A blueprint that describes an object's structure. - **Console pane**: A pane of RStudio used for interactively running R commands and viewing their output. - **Core tidyverse package**: Packages that are attached with `library(tidyverse)`. - **csv file**: A file stored in the "comma separated values" format. This describes a plain text file where commas separate values and each record (e.g., row in a data frame) is placed on a new line. - **Data frame**: A two-dimensional, heterogeneous data object comprised of equal-length vectors (a restrictive type of list under-the-hood). - **Data object**: Containers for values that structure references in an ordered, predictable way. - **Dimensions**: The arrangement of values in an object; may also refer to the number of values or child objects within a given dimension (i.e., rows or columns) - **Double numeric vector**: An atomic numeric vector where the values are stored as decimal numbers (essentially). - **Environment**: A dimensionless data structure that contains references (names) to data stored in memory. - **Environment (of a function)**: The location of a function's variables. - **Escape character**: A backslash (`\`) placed before a character to tell R to treat that character literally rather than as part of R's syntax. - **Factor**: A value that maps character labels onto integers. - **Filtering**: The process of subsetting a data frame's rows by a logical condition, most often with `filter()`. - **Function**: A set of instructions (stored as an R object) used to complete a given task. - **Global environment**: A workspace that provides a reference point for all user-assigned objects associated with the current session. - **Heterogeneous object**: A container that holds values of one or more object classes. - **Homogeneity**: Whether an object may contain one or more than one class of object. - **Homogeneous object**: a container that holds values of only one class. - **Index**: The location of a value or component object within a parent object. This term can also be used as a verb to describe the process of indexing. - **Indexing**: The process of subsetting an object by the position (location) of a value or component within it. - **Infix function**: A function in which the name of the function is placed between the function's arguments. - **Install**: Download the data and functions from a package onto your computer. - **Integer**: A whole number, or an atomic vector of data stored as whole numbers. - **Labels**: Character values supplied to the labels argument of factor() to rename the levels as a factor is created. - **Levels**: The character values mapped to a factor's integer values. - **Library**: The location of a package on your computer. - **List**: A one-dimensional, heterogeneous data object that can hold values or objects of any class. - **List item**: A data object contained within a list. - **Logical constant**: `TRUE` or `FALSE`. - **Logical operator**: An operator used to test a logical statement (e.g., `3 > 2`). - **Matrix**: A two-dimensional, homogeneous data object arranged into rows and columns (an atomic vector under-the-hood). - **Memory**: A temporary storage location for instructions (functions) and data. - **Metapackage**: A package that is comprised of more than one smaller packages. - **Name**: A symbol that R evaluates to retrieve the object associated with it through a binding in an environment. - **Nested function**: A function that is run inside of another function. - **Object**: A collection of one or more values or functions. - **Observation**: The full set of values measured on the same observational unit across attributes. - **One-dimensional object**: Objects where data are arranged in a single line. - **Operator**: A function expressed that is expressed as a symbol and is not followed by parentheses. - **Order**: The position of values (or child objects) within a data object. - **Package**: A set of pre-written functions that can be downloaded (*note: There are also data packages!*) - **Package environment**: A collection of variable names associated with objects in a package. - **Parent**: An object or environment that contains references to other objects. - **Placeholder symbol**: In the context of piping, the symbol that defines the location in the right-hand-side function where the piped data will be inserted (a period, `.`, for the *magrittr* pipe). - **Prefix function**: A function in which the name of the function precedes the target of the evaluation. - **Primitive function**: A function written in C code and made available to use through the base R package. - **Project**: A collection of files that is referenced by a `.RProj` file. - **R session**: A running R process and its current state. - **RDS file**: A storage format for data sets that are written in, and written for, program R. - **Recursive assignments**: Names within a data object (a list or data frame), as opposed to names within the global environment. - **Recursive object**: An object made up of references to other, nested objects (e.g., a list). - **Reference tree**: A visualization of the storage locations and names of parent and child objects. - **Relative file path**: The path to a file on your hard drive relative to the current working directory. - **Script**: A text file that contains a set of commands to read, manipulate, and analyze data. - **Session**: The time spent and operations conducted since opening R. - **Session history**: All lines of code that have been sent to R since the beginning of a session (or since the session history was last cleared). - **Snake_case**: A naming convention in which all letters are lowercase and words are separated with an underscore (`_`). - **Source pane**: A pane of RStudio used for writing, editing, and running scripts. - **String**: A character value comprised of more than one symbol. - **Structure**: The dimensionality, homogeneity, and storage class of a data object (may also describe its metadata). - **Subsetting**: Reduce a data object to a component or components of interest. - **Tab**: Each pane has a tab on the top of it. For example, I will often refer to the Environment or History tabs of the workspace pane. - **Tibble**: A type of data frame with additional properties that make it especially useful. - **Two-dimensional object**: An object where data are arranged as rows and columns. - **Type**: How an object is stored in your computer. - **Variable**: The full set of values that measure the same underlying attribute across observational units. - **Vector**: A one-dimensional object. - **Version history**: Changes to a package since its inception. - **Viewer pane**: A pane of RStudio used for navigating your system's files, viewing help files, and images/plot output (and more) - **Workspace pane**: A pane of RStudio used to view/manage objects in your global environment and your session history. ::: ::: panel **Important!** Primitive functions, as well as functions in the packages that R attaches by default (e.g., *base*, *utils*, *stats*, and *graphics*), are available as soon as you start an R session. ::: function_table ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
